decisions.where: tasks.md Group 1, new unchecked task; spec.md requirement 'Pending client mutations are flushed before the document is discarded'
decisions.summary: The debounced-save crash window gets an owning task. Flush the pending envelope at document discard with ONE fetch(..., { method: 'PUT', keepalive: true }) on the existing route and the existing { envelope, baseVersion } body.
decisions.triggers: pagehide, and visibilitychange when document.visibilityState === 'hidden'. beforeunload deliberately EXCLUDED -- it fires nowhere pagehide does not and registering it disqualifies the page from the back/forward cache, a regression in a fix whose purpose is not losing state.
decisions.mechanismRationale: navigator.sendBeacon is POST-only and the route 405s anything but GET/PUT/DELETE, so a beacon would require a new POST surface for no gain; keepalive fetch preserves the route, the body shape, and the baseVersion CAS.
decisions.boundedness: clear the armed timer first, fire one request, no retry, no queued follow-up, response never read.
decisions.neverLosesAnAcknowledgedRevision: The flush is explicitly NOT an acknowledgement: it does not clear dirty, does not advance baseVersion, does not call applySavedRecord. A losing flush is rejected by the server CAS rather than overwriting the winner, and the next load re-validates the cache against the head per task 1.3. This is why an unread response cannot corrupt the client's notion of the acknowledged revision.
decisions.skipConditions: not dirty; and isCoopCampaign true -- the same exemption markDirtyAction already applies, because a second writer there is the recorded co-op dual-writer 409 residual, not a rescued mutation.
decisions.residualNoteCorrected: The 2026-08-21 residual note's pointer ('belongs to the cutover-era client rewiring (5.7 scope)') is corrected in place to name task 1.6, recording honestly that 5.7 landed 2026-08-23 without claiming this fix, so the window had no owning task between those dates.

decisions.title: Contract-market offers are already source-record facts; 6.2's 'stored offer' is that persisted market promoted into the 6.1 private baseline
decisions.summary: Offers become source-owned by promoting the contractMarket that already lives in the persisted SerializedCampaign body into task 6.1's private baseline (which captures exactly that body under the P0a prepared transaction). 6.2's offer read is a contractId lookup in that captured baseline's contractMarket.offers. No new table, no persistence endpoint, no market event, no new field on any wire type.
decisions.consistencyWithD12: The market gains no audience it did not already have as a row in the campaigns table; it is never named by a wire-bearing type, which is exactly D12's source-only rule.
decisions.freshnessObligationCreated: Because the market reaches the source only through the debounced PUT, a command submitted inside that window names an offer the captured baseline does not hold. 6.2a therefore requires (server) a typed refusal distinct from every rules refusal when the contractId is absent from the baseline market, with NO fallback to a caller-supplied contract body, and (client) an acknowledged save before submitting, using the store's existing saveCampaign action. Task 1.6 is explicitly NOT a substitute: it fires at discard, not at market generation.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Carry offers on the journal or the wire -- either a ContractOffered event carrying the offer, or a compact offer-id fact with detail elsewhere.
rejectionGrounds: The event form is a direct D12 violation: full IContract inside a campaignEvent payload is by construction a restricted-guest-visible fact.

The compact-id form buys nothing: an id with no name and no employerId still leaves 6.2's server-derived name/employer with nothing to read, so the source-record lookup happens anyway and the wire fact is pure overhead.

Either form is a new campaign event type: reducer, D3 scope stamp at every emission site, and the change's QC pin ripple, for a fact with no guest audience and no consumer outside the source (the same simplest-solution ground on which D12 rejected the redactor).
It creates a SECOND durable home for the market beside the SerializedCampaign row that already holds it; single-source is cheaper than perpetual reconciliation.

decisions.questionPosed: explicit accepted transitional state with the reconciliation obligation assigned to a named task, OR a SHALL
decisions.chosen: SHALL -- spec.md requirement 'An accepted contract is written exactly once, by exactly one writer', with task 6.2b named as its owner in tasks.md and in D13
decisions.justification: A tolerated dual write is precisely the divergence the requirement forbids, and its failure mode is silent: once 6.2 commits an event AND the client keeps applying locally, the source record and the compact ledger disagree with nothing detecting it. The SHALL is also satisfiable INSIDE the admitted prefix rather than deferred -- 6.1's contract-only replay fold already produces the updated source record from the committed acceptance, so ICampaign.missions/contractMarket and the compact contracts come from ONE commit; and the refusal path (campaign-not-on-journal-authority, the common case while the flag is false) keeps the property trivially with today's single client-side write. A transitional tolerance would have licensed the parallel disconnected write path the admission brief flags as the gap.
decisions.minimality: Stated as one requirement with three scenarios (committed path, refused path, offer-not-durable refusal) rather than as a second requirement plus a transitional note; the offer-durability obligation rides the third scenario instead of a separate requirement.

scenarios: A committed acceptance produces both projections from one commit
A refused acceptance leaves exactly one client write
An offer the source record does not hold is refused, never trusted from the caller
The first acceptance on a campaign reads its market without a prior private payload
